extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, Office legal staff, and patent practitioners (patent owners/attorneys) involved in reissue and reexamination practice
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and examiner/practitioner guidance for when and how a reissue application and an ex parte reexamination proceeding for the same patent are merged, stayed, or otherwise coordinated, including filing, notification, amendment, fee, litigation, and certificate procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt OPLA notification and file delivery when reissue filed during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reissue application is filed during the pendency of a reexamination proceeding, OPLA should be notified as promptly as possible after the reissue application reaches the TC; if any of the reexamination file, the reissue application, and the patent file are paper files, they should be hand delivered to OPLA at the time of the notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification should occur immediately after the reissue application reaches the Technology Center; paper files should be hand-delivered when applicable to assist timely consideration of merger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of decision to merge or stay
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision on whether the proceedings are to be merged, or which proceeding (if any) is to be stayed, will generally be made as promptly as possible after receipt of the notification to OPLA and delivery of any paper files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Until a decision is mailed merging the proceedings or staying one, both proceedings continue and are conducted simultaneously but separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office may issue certificate at reexamination termination despite copending filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may, in certain situations, issue a certificate at the termination of a reexamination prosecution even if a copending reissue application or another reexamination request has already been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merger or other procedural action does not necessarily prevent issuance of a reexamination certificate at termination if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case-by-case merger/stay discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision on whether to merge the proceedings or stay a proceeding will be made on a case-by-case basis based upon the status of the various proceedings; the decision is within the sole discretion of the Office to facilitate orderly operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the status of the reissue application examination and the reexamination proceeding in making the merger/stay decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay determination when reissue about to issue and reexamination requested
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reissue patent will issue before the 3-month period for determination on the reexamination request has expired, the determination should normally be delayed until after granting of the reissue patent; any reexamination ordered would be on the reissue patent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reexamination is ordered after reissue issues, reexamination should proceed on reissue claims, and the reissue claims used must be presented as a "clean copy" (bracketed words removed; added words plain). Use form paragraph 22.05 to indicate proceedings are based on reissue claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination clean copy rules when based on reissue claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination starting point must be presented as a "clean copy" of the reissue patent claims: bracketed words in reissue claims should not appear in the reexamination clean copy; words added via the reissue appear plain (not italic) in the reexamination clean copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the changes made by reissue as the text of the patent; all bracketing/underlining with respect to the reissued patent should be converted per reexamination clean copy rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph for reexamination based on reissue claims (¶ 22.05)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the reissue patent has issued, the determination on the request for reexamination should specifically point out that the determination has been made on the claims of the reissue patent and not on the claims of the original patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ¶ 22.05 wording: e.g., note surrender of original patent and that subsequent proceedings are based on reissue patent claims; see MPEP for exact bracketed form paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy to merge narrower reexamination with broader reissue when expedient
rubrics_metrics.description: The general policy is to merge the more narrow reexamination proceeding with the broader reissue application examination whenever desirable to expedite the conduct of both proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the status of the reissue examination at the time the reexamination order is mailed; e.g., if reissue hasn't begun or hasn't been appealed, merging is likely; if reissue is on appeal to the Board/courts, consider staying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to place identical claims in merged proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: If a merger is ordered, the order will require that the patent owner place the same claims in the reissue application and in the reexamination proceeding for purposes of the merged proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amendment may be required to accomplish this within a specified time set in the order merging the proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stay of reexamination when reissue examination progressed
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reissue application examination has progressed to a point where merger is not desirable, the reexamination proceeding will generally be stayed until the reissue application examination is complete on the issues then pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After reissue examination completes on those issues, the reexamination may be removed and proceedings merged if reissue remains pending, or reexamination conducted separately if reissue abandoned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuance of reissue patent serves as reexamination certificate when merged
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reissue application examination and the reexamination proceeding are merged, the issuance of the reissue patent will also serve as the certificate under 37 CFR 1.570 and the reissue patent will so indicate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merged proceedings are conducted under reissue examination rules, and the reissue patent acts as the reexamination certificate where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt OPLA notification when reexamination underway and reissue filed
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reissue application is filed after an ex parte reexamination request has been filed or after reexamination ordered, OPLA should be notified as promptly as possible after the reissue application reaches the TC that the proceedings are ready for consideration of merger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If files are paper, they should be hand delivered to OPLA at the time of notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of issues and status when deciding merger after reexamination underway
rubrics_metrics.description: In deciding whether to merge the reissue application examination and the reexamination proceeding, consideration will be given as to whether issues are raised in the reissue application for consideration and to the status of the reexamination proceeding (e.g., appeal to Board or courts, Notice of Intent to Issue Reexamination Certificate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reexamination is on appeal or near completion, that fact may weigh against merger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner assignment for merged proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: With respect to appropriate examiner assignment of the merged reexamination/reissue proceeding, see MPEP § 2236.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP § 2236 for assignment rules and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance of identical amendments in merged proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where merger is ordered, the patent owner is required to maintain identical amendments in the reissue application and the reexamination file for purposes of the merged proceeding for as long as the proceedings remain merged (37 CFR 1.565(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If identical amendments are not present at merger, the patent owner must submit a "housekeeping" amendment placing the same amendments in both proceedings; the housekeeping amendment must not address patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Housekeeping amendments submitted under reissue practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments in a merged reexamination/reissue proceeding are submitted under 37 CFR 1.173, in accordance with reissue practice (see MPEP § 1453).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Housekeeping amendments should not raise patentability issues and must comply with reissue amendment procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRU/TC QAS jurisdiction when amendment time provided
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the merger decision gives the patent owner one month to provide an amendment to make the claims the same in each file, the CRU SPRS or TC QAS will retain jurisdiction over the reexamination proceeding to await submission of the amendment or expiration of the time to submit the amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After amendment is received and processed or time expires, the merged proceeding will be returned to the examiner to issue an Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner should prepare most advanced Office action for merged proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: Once returned to the examiner for issuance of an Office action, the examiner should prepare an Office action at the most advanced point possible for the first proceeding; if first proceeding ready for final rejection and second provides no new information, issue a final rejection for the merged proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to advance prosecution efficiently; consider both proceedings' statuses when selecting the form of action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indefiniteness rejection if housekeeping amendment not timely submitted
rubrics_metrics.description: If a housekeeping amendment to make the claims the same in each file is required by the merger decision but is not timely submitted, any claim that does not contain identical text in all of the merged proceedings should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, as being indefinite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely submission of identical claim text is mandatory to avoid indefiniteness rejections in merged files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply reissue statute/rules/case law to merged examination
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reissue application examination and a reexamination proceeding are merged, the merged examination will be conducted on the basis of the rules relating to the broader reissue application examination; the examiner will apply the reissue statute, rules, procedures, and case law to the merged proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is appropriate because reissue examination provisions include provisions equivalent to 35 U.S.C. 305 related to reexamination conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single Office action for merged proceedings and file entry
rubrics_metrics.description: In any merged reissue application and reexamination proceeding, each Office action issued by the examiner will take the form of a single action which jointly applies to both the reissue application and the reexamination proceeding; each action will contain identifying data for both and be physically entered into both files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain synchronized records across both files; ensure consistent content and indexing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single duplicate response requirement and service to third-party requester
rubrics_metrics.description: Any response by the applicant/patent owner in a merged proceeding must consist of a single response, filed in duplicate for entry in both files (or provide multiple copies if multiple reexamination proceedings being merged), and service of a copy must be made on any third party reexamination requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of all Office actions will be mailed to the third-party reexamination requester but not to other third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic dissolution of merger for failure to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant/patent owner in a merged proceeding fails to file a timely and appropriate response to any Office action, then the merger will be automatically dissolved (severed). The reissue application will be held abandoned; an NIRC will be issued, and the Director will proceed to issue a reexamination certificate under 37 CFR 1.570 in accordance with the last action of the Office unless further action is clearly needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely responses are essential to maintain merged status; abandonment consequences are significant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of express abandonment or CPA on merged proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant/patent owner files an express abandonment of the reissue application pursuant to 37 CFR 1.138, the next Office action will accept the express abandonment, dissolve the merged proceeding, and continue the reexamination proceeding; a CPA filing for a reissue design application may also result in dissolution of the merged proceeding, stay of the CPA, and separate continued prosecution of the reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing choices by patent owner (abandonment, CPA) have direct procedural consequences for merged proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of RCE on merged proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant/patent owner files a request for continued examination (RCE) of the reissue application under 37 CFR 1.114, then the merger will be automatically dissolved (severed), and the reissue application will be suspended; patent owners are put on notice that RCE practice is not available in reexamination and reexamination responses must account for that.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An RCE terminates merger and suspends the reissue application; failing to account for non-availability of RCE in reexamination responses can lead to termination under 37 CFR 1.550(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal/addition of grounds upon dissolution based on abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the merged proceeding is dissolved based on abandonment of the reissue application and the reexamination proceeding continues, any grounds of rejection not applicable under reexamination (e.g., based on public use or on sale) should be withdrawn and any new grounds applicable under reexamination (e.g., improper broadened claims) should be made by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should note any questions remaining which cannot be considered under reexamination pursuant to 37 CFR 1.552(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: No premature petitions to merge or stay before reexamination order
rubrics_metrics.description: No petition to merge the reissue application and the reexamination proceeding, or to stay one of them because of the other, should be filed before an order granting reexamination is issued because the Office will generally, sua sponte, make a decision to merge or stay; premature petitions will not be considered and will be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevent premature filings relating to reexamination proceedings; decisions prior to reexamination order will be expunged from the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner petition to merge or stay after 1.530 statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 to merge the reissue application and the reexamination proceeding, or to stay one of them because of the other, at the time the patent owner’s statement under 37 CFR 1.530 is filed or subsequent thereto if the Office has not acted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions by the patent owner will be considered; after the order for reexamination these petitions are referred to OPLA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party requester lacks standing to petition to merge reissue application
rubrics_metrics.description: A third-party reexamination requester does not have a right to file a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 to merge a reexamination proceeding and a reissue application (the requester cannot be a party to a reissue application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instead, a third-party requester may file a notification of concurrent proceedings pursuant to MPEP § 2282; petitions to merge filed by parties other than the patent owner will be returned or expunged, although the requester may petition to stay the reexamination proceeding it requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-order petitions to OPLA
rubrics_metrics.description: All petitions to merge or stay which are filed by the patent owner or the third-party requester subsequent to the date of the order for reexamination will be referred to OPLA for decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPLA has authority to decide petitions filed after the reexamination order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-fee payment in merged proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the proceedings have been merged and a paper is filed which requires payment of a fee (e.g., excess claim fee, extension of time fee, petition fee, appeal fee, brief fee, oral hearing fee), only a single fee need be paid for the merged proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: only one appeal brief fee is required even if the brief relates to merged multiple proceedings; ensure required copies are provided as necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited handling where court-ordered or litigation stayed
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request for ex parte reexamination is filed as a result of a court order or litigation agreement sanctioned by a court, or litigation is stayed for filing of the reexamination request, all aspects of the proceeding will be expedited to the extent possible; if reexamination is ordered, post-statement examination/reply will be expedited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with litigation schedule and expedite review and responses where court involvement mandates acceleration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of known federal court decision at time of determination
rubrics_metrics.description: If a federal court decision on the merits of a patent is known to the examiner at the time the determination on the ex parte reexamination request is made, the examiner must follow guidance: a court's decision does not necessarily mean no substantial new question (SNQ) exists because the Office uses different standards of proof and claim interpretation; non-final holdings are not controlling; a final holding of invalidity/unenforceability is controlling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should accord deference to factual findings of the court where evidence is the same but determine independently whether an SNQ exists; examples and case citations (Trans Texas, Translogic, Swanson, Baxter) illustrate the principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-court-decision review by CRU SPRS
rubrics_metrics.description: Any determination on a request for reexamination which the examiner makes after a federal court decision must be reviewed by the Central Reexamination Unit (CRU) Supervisory Patent Reexamination Specialist (SPRS) to ensure conformity with current Office litigation policy and guidelines (see MPEP § 2240).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referral to CRU SPRS ensures consistent treatment of cases involving parallel litigation and court decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination deadlines when reexamination precedes court decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Where reexamination is ordered prior to a federal court decision and the 3-month statutory period for determination applies, the determination will be made within 3 months based on the record before the examiner without awaiting the court decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner has an obligation under 37 CFR 1.565(a) to promptly notify the Office of any prior or concurrent proceedings and any court decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of federal court decisions issued after reexamination order
rubrics_metrics.description: If a federal court decision issues while reexamination is pending, the order to reexamine is reviewed to determine whether an SNQ still exists; if no SNQ, the reexamination is terminated. Non-final court decisions have no binding effect on reexamination; a final holding that claims are not invalid also is not binding, but a final holding of invalidity or unenforceability (after all appeals) is binding and such claims are withdrawn from reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 22.20 to note claims held invalid by court and not being reexamined; continue reexamination as to remaining claims if any.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner duty to investigate litigation and notify supervisory review
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner is responsible for conducting a reasonable investigation for evidence that the patent has been or is involved in litigation — including reviewing the reexamination file, patent file, and litigation computer search; if litigation or a court decision is discovered, the examiner must bring the matter to the attention of the CRU SPRS or TC QAS prior to further action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRU SPRS or TC QAS must review any action taken by the examiner in such circumstances to ensure current Office litigation policy is followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal court decision controlling for claims finally held invalid
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a federal court has ruled upon the merits of a patent and an ex parte reexamination is still appropriate under guidelines, the federal court decision will be considered controlling and followed as to claims finally held to be invalid by the court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims finally held invalid or unenforceable are withdrawn from reexamination; reexamination continues as to remaining claims not held invalid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with PTAB review proceedings (AIA reviews)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under AIA amendments (35 U.S.C. 315(d), 325(d)), during the pendency of an inter partes review, post grant review, or covered business method review, the Director may determine how the PTAB review and other Office proceedings may proceed (stay, transfer, consolidation, termination). If an examiner becomes aware of a PTAB review for the same patent that is being reexamined, the ex parte reexamination must be referred to the examiner’s SPRS, and the SPRS will coordinate with the PTAB before taking action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awareness of PTAB proceedings does not change the statutory three-month decision requirement for a reexamination request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of Notice of Intent to Issue Reexamination Certificate (NIRC) upon conclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon conclusion of the ex parte reexamination proceeding, the examiner must prepare a "Notice of Intent to Issue Ex Parte Reexamination Certificate" (NIRC) by completing form PTOL-469; where claims are found patentable, reasons must be given for each claim found patentable; prepare reexamination file so Office of Data Management can prepare and issue a certificate under 35 U.S.C. 307 and 37 CFR 1.570.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRU SPRS/TC QAS will convene a panel review conference; conference members will review patentability and initial the NIRC. If conference does not confirm patentability, the examiner will reevaluate and issue an appropriate Office action rejecting the claims. A panel review is not held for any claim that was in the case when reviewed by the Board or a federal court.
